Quotas & billing {{ds:component/chip|label=v2|variant=primary}}

Godzilla accounts operate under usage quotas determined by your plan tier. Quotas apply at the workspace level across API request throughput, monthly event volume, and concurrent pipeline resources.

Plan tiers

Each workspace is assigned to a tier that dictates default rate limits and monthly event capacities.

Plan Rate limit Monthly events Active pipelines Support SLA
Starter 100 req / min 50,000 3 Community
Standard 1,000 req / min 1,000,000 25 1 business day
Enterprise Custom (10,000+ req / min) Custom / Unlimited Unlimited 24/7 dedicated SLA

What happens when you exceed a quota

Exceeding limits is handled differently depending on whether you exceed a per-minute API request rate or a monthly event volume quota.

API rate limits (HTTP 429)

If your application sends more requests in a one-minute window than your tier allows, the API returns a 429 Too Many Requests status code. Responses include a Retry-After header indicating how many seconds to wait before resuming requests. See Rate limits & errors for header details and retry strategies.

Monthly event quotas

Monthly event usage resets on the first day of your billing cycle. When approaching or exceeding event limits:

  • 80% and 100% threshold alerts: Account admins receive email notifications and webhook lifecycle events (workspace.quota_warning) when approaching your limit.
  • Standard plan overages: On the Standard tier, pipelines continue running without interruption. Overage events are billed at $0.15 per 10,000 events on your next invoice.
  • Starter plan cap: Starter tier workspaces pause pipeline ingestion once the 50,000 event limit is reached until the next billing cycle or an upgrade to Standard.

Resource limits (pipelines and connectors)

If you attempt to create more active pipelines or connectors than your plan allows, the API returns a 403 Forbidden with code quota_exceeded.

Upgrading and quota increases

You can upgrade your plan or add billing details directly from workspace settings. If your workload requires higher burst rate limits or tailored enterprise terms, reach out via Support / Contact.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Monitoring usage|body_html=

Check your current monthly event consumption and active pipeline counts anytime in the workspace dashboard or via the workspace metadata endpoint.

1. Pagination: offset → cursor

v1 used page/per_page query parameters. v2 uses an opaque cursor and next_cursor — see Rate limits & errors for the exact envelope.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=diff|language=diff|code=- GET /v1/pipelines?page=2&per_page=20 + GET /v2/pipelines?cursor=eyJvZmZzZXQiOjIwfQ}}

v1 had no push notifications — you polled a pipeline's status endpoint. v2 replaces this with the Webhooks endpoint: subscribe to pipeline.completed and pipeline.failed instead of polling.

3. Error shape

v1 returned bare error strings. v2 wraps every error in an object with a stable code field. Update any error handling that matched on message text — see the error shape reference.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=v1 is retired|body_html=

v1 endpoints no longer accept requests. If you're seeing 404s on /v1/* paths, that's why — there is no grace-period fallback.

}}

Common migration issues are covered in Troubleshooting / FAQ.

Backfilling lets you stream historical data from your storage or database into downstream targets — bootstrapping new destinations, backpopulating historical records, or replaying data after schema changes.

1. Define a time-bounded source connector

Configure your source connector with start and end timestamps (or watermarks) to define the historical boundary. This prevents the backfill job from processing live events prematurely.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=backfill-source.json|language=json|code={ "type": "postgres", "direction": "source", "config": { "connection_string": "postgres://user:secret@db.example.com:5432/production", "query": "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2025-01-01T00:00:00Z' AND created_at < '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'", "timestamp_column": "created_at" } }}}

2. Set batch size and concurrency controls

Historical backfills often involve large data volumes. Adjust your pipeline's batch size and concurrency limit to avoid exhausting memory or triggering rate limits on your destination system.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=pipeline-backfill.json|language=json|code={ "name": "orders-backfill-2025", "source_connector_id": "conn_pg_orders_backfill", "destination_connector_id": "conn_snowflake_dw", "settings": { "batch_size": 5000, "concurrency": 4, "max_retries": 5 } }}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Destination throughput|body_html=

Handling errors & retries

Every event that fails a transform or a destination write is retried automatically. This guide covers how that works and what to do when retries run out.

Automatic retries

Failed events retry with exponential backoff — 1s, 2s, 4s, up to a per-pipeline configurable ceiling. Most transient failures (a destination hiccup, a rate-limited third party) resolve within the first few attempts.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=pipeline-retry-config.json|language=json|code={ "retry_policy": { "max_attempts": 5, "backoff": "exponential", "initial_delay_ms": 1000 } }}}

Dead-lettering

An event that exhausts its retries is moved to that pipeline's dead-letter queue rather than dropped silently.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=Dead-lettered events don't retry themselves|body_html=

Once in the dead-letter queue, an event stays there until you replay it or explicitly discard it — it will not retry again on its own.

}}

Replaying events

Use the Events endpoint's replay action to re-run a specific dead-lettered event once the underlying issue is fixed.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=replay.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/events/evt_8f2c1a90/replay \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY"}}

Watching for failures

Subscribe to pipeline.failed via Webhooks so you find out about dead-lettered events before a customer does. See also Monitoring & alerts.

Connectors endpoint {{ds:component/chip|label=v2|variant=primary}}

Manage connectors — the source and destination integrations pipelines read from and write to.

Create a connector

POST /v2/connectors

Rotate credentials

{{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Shared connectors|body_html=

A connector referenced by multiple pipelines is rotated once, for all of them. Check a connector's pipeline_count field before rotating during a busy window.

}}

Health status

Schemas

A schema is a declarative contract that defines the expected structure, data types, and required fields for an event payload moving through a pipeline. Schemas prevent malformed records from propagating downstream and ensure data integrity across source and destination connectors.

Declaring a schema

Godzilla schemas follow standard JSON Schema (Draft-07) specifications. You define schemas per event type or attach them directly to pipeline ingress and egress stages.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=order-created.schema.json|language=json|code={ "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", "title": "OrderCreatedPayload", "type": "object", "properties": { "order_id": { "type": "string" }, "customer_id": { "type": "string" }, "amount_cents": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 }, "currency": { "type": "string", "enum": ["USD", "EUR", "GBP"] }, "status": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["order_id", "amount_cents", "currency"], "additionalProperties": false }}}

Validation & enforcement modes

When a pipeline processes an event, Godzilla validates the payload against the registered schema. You can configure how validation failures are handled using one of three enforcement modes:

  • strict — Any event failing validation is immediately rejected and routed to the pipeline's dead-letter queue.
  • warn — The event continues through the pipeline, but a platform warning event is emitted for monitoring and alerting.
  • drop — Invalid events are silently discarded without halting pipeline execution or triggering retries.
{{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Validation failure handling|body_html=

In strict mode, validation errors do not retry endlessly. Because payload schema mismatches are deterministic, failed events bypass transient retries and move straight to the dead-letter queue. See Handling errors & retries for details on inspecting and replaying dead-lettered events.

}}

Schema validation in the pipeline lifecycle

Validation can occur at three points in a pipeline run:

  1. Ingress validation — Verified immediately after a source connector emits an event, ensuring source data conforms to expectations.
  2. Post-transform validation — Verified after transform steps run to confirm reshaped payloads match target specifications.
  3. Egress validation — Checked before writing to a destination connector to guarantee downstream compatibility.

Schema evolution & compatibility

As business requirements change, schemas evolve. Godzilla supports backward and forward compatibility rules to prevent breaking active pipelines:

  • Additive changes — Adding optional fields is backward-compatible and does not require pipeline downtime.
  • Breaking changes — Removing fields or adding new required fields requires creating a new pipeline version or using a transform step to migrate payload shapes.

Quotas & billing {{ds:component/chip|label=v2|variant=primary}}

Godzilla accounts operate under usage quotas determined by your plan tier. Quotas apply at the workspace level across API request throughput, monthly event volume, and concurrent pipeline resources.

Plan tiers

Each workspace is assigned to a tier that dictates default rate limits and monthly event capacities.

Plan Rate limit Monthly events Active pipelines Support SLA
Starter 100 req / min 50,000 3 Community
Standard 1,000 req / min 1,000,000 25 1 business day
Enterprise Custom (10,000+ req / min) Custom / Unlimited Unlimited 24/7 dedicated SLA

What happens when you exceed a quota

Exceeding limits is handled differently depending on whether you exceed a per-minute API request rate or a monthly event volume quota.

API rate limits (HTTP 429)

If your application sends more requests in a one-minute window than your tier allows, the API returns a 429 Too Many Requests status code. Responses include a Retry-After header indicating how many seconds to wait before resuming requests. See Limits, quotas & errors for header details and retry strategies.

Monthly event quotas

Monthly event usage resets on the first day of your billing cycle. When approaching or exceeding event limits:

  • 80% and 100% threshold alerts: Account admins receive email notifications and webhook lifecycle events (workspace.quota_warning) when approaching your limit.
  • Standard plan overages: On the Standard tier, pipelines continue running without interruption. Overage events are billed at $0.15 per 10,000 events on your next invoice.
  • Starter plan cap: Starter tier workspaces pause pipeline ingestion once the 50,000 event limit is reached until the next billing cycle or an upgrade to Standard.

Resource limits (pipelines and connectors)

If you attempt to create more active pipelines or connectors than your plan allows, the API returns a 403 Forbidden with code quota_exceeded.

Upgrading and quota increases

You can upgrade your plan or add billing details directly from workspace settings. If your workload requires higher burst rate limits or tailored enterprise terms, reach out via Support / Contact.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Monitoring usage|body_html=

Check your current monthly event consumption and active pipeline counts anytime in the workspace dashboard or via the workspace metadata endpoint.

}} {{ds:component/docs-toc|items_html=

args.body:
Glossary

Short definitions for every term used throughout these docs.

Pipeline
A named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector, through optional transforms, to a destination connector.
Connector
A pre-built integration to an external system — a source, a destination, or both.
Event
The atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, or a platform lifecycle notification like pipeline.failed.
Schema
A declarative contract specifying the structure, types, and validation rules for event payloads.
Webhook
An outbound HTTP request Godzilla sends to a URL you control when a subscribed event occurs.
Dead-letter queue
Where an event goes after exhausting its retries, rather than being dropped. See Handling errors & retries.
Cursor pagination
The pagination style used by every v2 list endpoint. See Limits, quotas & errors.
Quota
Usage allowances assigned to a workspace based on its plan tier, covering request throughput and monthly event volume. See Quotas & billing.
Workspace
The top-level account boundary an API key is scoped to.

args.short_description: Common problems and fixes across pipelines, connectors, and webhooks.
args.body:
Troubleshooting / FAQ

Common problems, and where in the docs to go for the full explanation.

My pipeline isn't processing events

Check the source connector's health field via the Connectors endpoint. A down connector stalls every pipeline that reads from it. If it's healthy, confirm the pipeline itself is active and not paused — see Scheduling & triggers.

Events keep failing and landing in the dead-letter queue

Walk through Handling errors & retries — it covers both diagnosing the failure and replaying events once fixed.

I'm not receiving webhook deliveries

Verify your endpoint returns a 2xx status and that you're checking X-Godzilla-Signature correctly — a rejected signature looks identical to a dropped delivery from the outside. Full details in the Webhooks endpoint reference.

I'm getting 429s

You've hit the standard-tier limit described in Limits, quotas & errors. Back off using the Retry-After header, or review Quotas & billing to learn about plan tiers and how overages are handled.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Migrating from v1?|body_html=

A number of \"it worked yesterday\" reports trace back to v1's offset pagination or polling patterns carried over into v2 code. See the Migration guide.

}}

Still stuck?

Reach the team via Support / Contact.

args.body:
Migration guide (v1 → v2) {{ds:component/chip|label=v1 retired|variant=danger}}

v1 reached end of life on 2026-08-01 alongside the webhooks GA changelog entry. This guide covers the three breaking changes you need to handle to move a v1 integration to v2.

1. Pagination: offset → cursor

v1 used page/per_page query parameters. v2 uses an opaque cursor and next_cursor — see Limits, quotas & errors for the exact envelope.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=diff|language=diff|code=- GET /v1/pipelines?page=2&per_page=20 + GET /v2/pipelines?cursor=eyJvZmZzZXQiOjIwfQ}}

2. Status checks: polling → webhooks

v1 had no push notifications — you polled a pipeline's status endpoint. v2 replaces this with the Webhooks endpoint: subscribe to pipeline.completed and pipeline.failed instead of polling.

3. Error shape

v1 returned bare error strings. v2 wraps every error in an object with a stable code field. Update any error handling that matched on message text — see the error shape reference.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=v1 is retired|body_html=

v1 endpoints no longer accept requests. If you're seeing 404s on /v1/* paths, that's why — there is no grace-period fallback.

}}

Still stuck?

Common migration issues are covered in Troubleshooting / FAQ.

input.body:
Migration guide (v1 → v2) {{ds:component/chip|label=v1 retired|variant=danger}}

v1 reached end of life on 2026-08-01 alongside the webhooks GA changelog entry. This guide covers the three breaking changes you need to handle to move a v1 integration to v2.

1. Pagination: offset → cursor

v1 used page/per_page query parameters. v2 uses an opaque cursor and next_cursor — see Limits, quotas & errors for the exact envelope.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=diff|language=diff|code=- GET /v1/pipelines?page=2&per_page=20 + GET /v2/pipelines?cursor=eyJvZmZzZXQiOjIwfQ}}

2. Status checks: polling → webhooks

v1 had no push notifications — you polled a pipeline's status endpoint. v2 replaces this with the Webhooks endpoint: subscribe to pipeline.completed and pipeline.failed instead of polling.

3. Error shape

v1 returned bare error strings. v2 wraps every error in an object with a stable code field. Update any error handling that matched on message text — see the error shape reference.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=v1 is retired|body_html=

v1 endpoints no longer accept requests. If you're seeing 404s on /v1/* paths, that's why — there is no grace-period fallback.

}}

Still stuck?

Common migration issues are covered in Troubleshooting / FAQ.
